title: Cross-Reference

illustrates.quote: These notes are formatted in the same way. a. Do not use a reference mark. b. Ignore font attributes except when they are necessary for distinction. c. A blank line precedes and follows the note to avoid the impression that it is “attached” to the previous or following paragraphs. d. When the note includes a heading, do not insert a blank line between the heading and the note. Use 7-7 margins for the heading. Transcribe the note on the next line using 5-5 margins. e. Use 7-5 margins for a note without a heading. f. Insert the notes at the most appropriate location on the page.

resolution: A and B transcribed identical `braille.lines` except A included a leading blank line (source .txt line 6800, a genuine 40-blank-cell braille line) that B omitted. Settled the same way as Example 9-4: byte-counted directly from the source, line 6800 carries the 8-space margin plus 40 literal U+2800 cells, distinct from the truly-empty .txt lines 6796-6799 before it -- A's leading blank is correct and kept. Print-content disagreement: A folded the icon and the note's own heading into one 'other' block's text; B kept the icon as its own 'other' block and gave 'Speaking Connection' its own 'heading' block (level null). Resolved to B's finer split (icon as 'other', note heading as its own 'heading' block, level 3/cell-7 measured directly from the agreed braille's own indent) since it separates print's own distinct visual elements rather than merging unrelated content into one block's text, matching this section's general convention (cf. example-9-8). Both runs agreed on the 'librarisn' typo, kept verbatim per the task's 'as printed' instruction.
